svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: iOS · Projects · sharing · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/ProjectsView.swift (header) + App/ProjectSharingChip.swift (ProjectSharingChip) over Shared/ProjectTransferServer.swift. The Projects list exactly as projects.portrait.svg draws it, plus the SHARING CHIP the header grows while this device is serving its library to another one over the local network — everything below the chip shifts down 48pt (a 38pt chip 10pt under the title) and nothing else changes. The chip is drawn ONLY while ProjectTransferServer.isRunning; with sharing off the screen is projects.portrait.svg unchanged, because a permanent "not sharing" row would remind every session of a feature most never touch. The server arms when the Projects tab appears and Settings ▸ Advanced ▸ "Share projects with nearby devices" (UserDefaults `transfer.sharingEnabled`, OFF by default) is on — a separate grant from "Allow remote access", because serving every project on the device and driving its shutter are different things to hand a stranger on the network. It stands down when the switch goes off, when the app backgrounds (iOS suspends network activity anyway; this only makes it honest), and when the chip is tapped. The code is minted fresh on every arm, so a code read off this screen an hour ago is not still valid, and it is shown 3+3 so it can be read off a phone on the desk and typed on the Mac without losing your place. Modelled on App/RemoteLinkChip.swift and deliberately somewhere else: that chip lives on the capture screen because the camera remote's code is regenerated every time that screen appears, whereas this one survives tab switches and navigation — which is the point of not hanging the server off a screen. TWO OTHER STATES, desc-only. Sending: a green arrow.up.circle.fill, "Sending Tram morning", "Stop" trailing, a second line reading "3,2 GB of 12,4 GB" and a 4pt accent progress bar under it (the counts are uncompressed and there is no compression on the payload path, so unlike the archive importer's bar this denominator is the truth rather than an estimate). Unavailable: an orange exclamationmark.triangle.fill, "Sharing unavailable" and the failure sentence — almost always a denied Local Network prompt, which otherwise presents as "nobody ever connects". Verified on the simulator 2026-08-27 with `transfer.sharingEnabled` seeded true and LL_TAB=projects; the Mac end is macOS/library-import.*.svg.
svg.text: mirrors App/ProjectSharingChip.swift — drawn only while sharing is armed; sending / unavailable states desc-only
